projectBackground.name: Rail Depot Programme — Maintenance Shed
projectBackground.context: A critical activity slipped. The contractor claims an extension of time and the authority wants the real impact.

manager.name: Helen Marsh
manager.note: The programme is a legal document. Be clear which activities are critical and what the delay actually does to completion.

assignment.title: Analyse the programme and the delay
assignment.brief: Run the forward pass, find the critical path and float, assess the delay and write an EOT note.

documents.name: Activity List
documents.note: A 5 days; B 7 days after A; C 10 days after A; D 4 days after B and C.

documents.name: Progress Update
documents.note: Activity C is forecast to take 4 days longer.

documents.name: Contract Clause
documents.note: Extension of time is granted for delay on the critical path caused by the employer.

tasks.title: Project Duration
tasks.prompt: A (5), B (7), C (10), D (4). A precedes B and C; D follows both. What is the project duration (days)?
tasks.reasoning: The longest path sets the duration.
tasks.mistake: Adding all durations (26) ignores parallel work.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Float on B
tasks.prompt: Using the same network, what is the total float on activity B (days)?
tasks.workingNote: Critical path is 19; B's path is 16; float = 3.
tasks.reasoning: Float is the delay an activity can absorb.
tasks.mistake: Treating B as critical wastes effort.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Delay Impact
tasks.prompt: If C takes 4 days longer, what is the new project duration (days)?
tasks.reasoning: A delay on the critical path moves completion day for day.
tasks.mistake: Assuming float absorbs the delay is wrong for C.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Logic Relationships
tasks.prompt: The most common relationship in Primavera P6 is:
tasks.tip: Use other types only with reason.
tasks.mistake: Overusing lags and SS/FF obscures the logic.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Forward Pass (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Early Finish in column D = C + B for each activity (ES given).
tasks.reasoning: D starts at 15 — the later of B (12) and C (15).
tasks.tip: Successor start equals the latest predecessor finish.
tasks.mistake: Taking the earlier predecessor understates duration.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: EOT Note
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence note assessing the extension-of-time request.
tasks.modelAnswer: Activity C is on the critical path (zero float) so a 4-day delay moves completion from day 19 to day 23. If the cause is an employer delay under the contract clause, the contractor is entitled to a 4-day extension of time. We have asked for the programme update showing the fragnet and the delay notice dates. Entitlement to costs is assessed separately.
tasks.reasoning: A good EOT note states the critical impact, the contractual basis and the evidence required.
tasks.mistake: Granting time without analysis creates liability.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Float That Disappeared
caseStudy.background: A contractor used all the float on a non-critical activity, then a small delay on another path became critical and finished late. Both sides disputed who owned the float.
caseStudy.solution: Sterling added a float-ownership clause and monthly programme audits.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Know your critical path and who owns float.
